namespace F1
def range (n : Nat) : List Nat := List.range n
def bound : Nat := 10
def P (i : Nat) : Prop := True
theorem allP (n : Nat) : ∀ i ∈ range n, P i := fun _ _ => trivial
theorem existsBig : ∃ k > bound, P k := ⟨11, by decide, trivial⟩
end F1

why: _KEYWORD_BINDER captures everything between the quantifier and the comma, so in `∀ i ∈ range n,` / `∃ k > bound,` the domain `range`, `n`, `bound` are treated as bound names and every occurrence of them in the signature is dropped. In Mathlib this hits every `∑ i ∈ range n, ...`, `∀ x ∈ univ`, `⋃ i ∈ Iio n` under `open Finset`/`open Set` (about 2,200 occurrences with unqualified Finset/Set domains).

def P (n : Nat) : Prop := True

why: _BRACKET_BINDER is run over the whole binder region, so the type ascription `(card α : Nat)` inside a hypothesis type is read as a binder `(card α : ...)`; `card` becomes a local name and the constant is never reported. Typical Mathlib form: `(h : (card s : ℝ) ≤ ...)`, `(h : (choose n k : ℚ) = ...)` under `open Finset`/`open Nat`.

files.Pkg/File.lean: theorem slow (hfun : True) (h : hfun                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                = hfun) : True := trivial

why: _KEYWORD_BINDER `\s+([^,:=⇒]*?)\s*(?:,|:|=>|↦)`: when the match fails (group hits `=` not followed by `>`), the greedy `\s+`, the lazy group and the trailing `\s*` all re-partition the same whitespace run, giving O(N^3) in the run length after a binder keyword (8x per doubling), and O(K·L) for K keywords without terminator. Correct output, harmless at real indentation widths (<1 ms below ~50 spaces); only pathological formatting triggers it. Fix: make the group start with a non-space (`\s+(\S[^,:=⇒]*?)?`) or use a possessive/atomic match.
